I’d go to work at the mall and feel oddly pumped, almost on top of the world one minute, then snapping at coworkers or my wife over nothing the next. I couldn’t sit still on shift—constantly pacing, checking every camera twice, volunteering to cover extra posts, starting “projects” at home I never finished. I even did some things I’m ashamed of—flirting heavily with a younger woman who works nights, and I ended up meeting someone from online behind my wife’s back. That’s really not like me, and it’s caused a lot of problems at home.

Then it kind of flipped. For the last three months, I’ve been dragging myself through the day. On my days off I mostly stay in the bedroom, ignoring calls from friends and my kids. I can sleep 12 hours, then doze in the recliner. My head feels stuffed with cotton—simple things, like filling out an incident report, feel confusing. Sometimes, especially when I’m on an upper level at work or waiting at a busy road, I get these sudden urges to just step off or walk into traffic. I don’t have a plan, but the thought hits me hard and scares me.

Through all of this I’ve been on edge—worrying about money, my job, my marriage—like my nerves never settle down, whether I’m “up” or “down.” It’s getting harder to do my rounds properly, and my wife says she doesn’t recognize me anymore.
